newsitem.title: FRANCE: Societe Generale sees strong first half.
newsitem.headline: Societe Generale sees strong first half.

text.p: Societe Generale chairman Marc Vienot forecast on Thursday that the French bank's 1997 first half gross operating income should be up significantly over the corresponding year-earlier period.
He said in a statement that consolidated net income should "show an even more significant rise over the first half of 1996."
Vienot said retail banking activities registered a "satisfactory level of growth" in deposits and assets under management.
Loans to individuals posted a significant increase thanks to greater volumes for mortgage and consumer credit but commercial loans were down due to low demand.
He added that Credit du Nord consolidated its 1996 recovery.
He said asset management showed strong growth in business. Assets under management totalled over 500 billion francs, a rise of 17 percent over the same period of 1996.
Group investment banking in France and abroad saw an improvement in all sectors.
Trading activities were "excellent" and corporate finance and commercial banking showed significant growth, he said.
During the first half, management of the group shareholdings portfolio remained active in a favourable stock market environment, he said.
The statement followed a board meeting on Wednesday.
First-half results are due to be approved at a board meeting on September 10, 1997.
